audience: a new driver, or the parent setting up a teen's first car, working through the first week with the keys
someone who just bought a used car, or inherited one, with no service records in the glove box
a two-car household where nobody can say which car is due for what
someone who dreads the shop counter and has been surprised by work they did not ask for
the owner who tows, drives short trips, or lives with dust, heat or cold
a seller about to list the car who wants to show it was looked after
the person who does the winter prep: battery, tires, wipers, the kit in the trunk

visualWorld.setting: Daylight in an ordinary driveway, a garage bay and the seat of the car, never a showroom and never a race track. The pins live in the objects an owner actually handles: the instrument cluster with its odometer, the dropped-open glove box, the clipboard at the shop counter, the manila key tag a shop hangs on your keys, the licence plate, the spiral log on the passenger seat, the frosted windscreen, the open trunk with the winter kit. The car itself is always a generic, unbranded shape (no badge, no grille logo, no real model). Nothing is ever drawn plugged into the car: no OBD dongle, no signal waves from car to phone, no lit check-engine lamp, because the product reads nothing from the vehicle.

props.draw: Instrument binnacle as a wide rounded rectangle in ink outline with a soft fill; two round dials left and right (thin tick marks around the arc, a needle as a tapered line with a small hub circle); in the centre a rectangular odometer window with six digit rollers, each a small rounded rect alternating paper and soft-accent fill, digits set in the monospace face; a tiny 'mi' label. No warning lamps lit.
Small half-circle dial with E and F at the ends, a few ticks, a needle; a pump glyph made of a rounded rect with a hose curve. Used only to say the person chose a fuel type, never as live data.

A road ribbon in graphite with a dashed accent centre line that winds down the pin in two or three soft S-curves; mile-marker posts along it as thin rectangles with a small rectangular sign on top, each sign carrying one timeline label; a tiny side-view car shape on the road near the top.

The top corner of a windscreen as a trapezoid of pale glass with one diagonal highlight stripe and a dark rubber edge; a small rounded-rect sticker stuck in the corner with an accent header band and two or three blank ruled lines (left blank: the pin never prints a service interval on it).

A band of dashboard in graphite with a rounded underside; below it a hatch dropped open at about 30 degrees, drawn as a trapezoid with a soft inner face and a slim chrome latch rectangle; the dark cavity behind as a rounded rect in ink at low opacity; contents fan out of it and overlap the hatch edge, each with a thin leader line to its label.
Rounded rectangle card in paper fill with an accent header stripe, a short bold line for the plate characters (drawn as blocks, no real plate), two thin muted lines, a tiny folded corner triangle.
Same card shape as registration-card but with a soft-accent fill, a small shield-free badge circle top left, three thin lines; slightly rotated to overlap the registration card.
A narrow card with a simple handset outline and one long blank line for a number, punched hole at the top corner.

Thick booklet seen at a slight angle: a rectangle cover with a darker spine band in accent, a simple generic car silhouette on the cover (rounded body, two wheels), a ribbon bookmark hanging out of the bottom as a narrow strip with a notched end; when open, two pages with ruled lines and a small three-column table.
Pen-style pressure gauge: a slim cylinder body in steel grey, an angled chuck head at one end (short angled rect with a round opening), a measuring rod sliding out of the other end with tick marks.

Front view of a tyre: a thick graphite ring, tread blocks as small rectangles notched around the outer circumference, a five-spoke rim in paper fill with a centre hub circle; a tread-depth gauge as a small T-shaped tool pressed into a groove.

A rounded box battery in graphite with an accent label band, two terminals as short cylinders marked + and minus; a white scalloped cap of frost along the top edge, three small icicle triangles hanging from the label band, two or three snowflake sparkles around it.

A long thin wiper arm pivoting from the bottom of a windscreen, the blade as a slightly thicker bar with a dark rubber edge; the glass behind covered in a pale frost texture (stippled dots) with one clean cleared arc where the blade has swept.
Plastic jug with an integrated handle loop and a screw cap; translucent soft fill with a wavy liquid line two-thirds up; a small windscreen-spray glyph on the label.

Rear of a hatchback with the tailgate raised (a tilted rounded panel above), the boot floor as a flat trapezoid holding: coiled jumper cables (two looping lines, one accent, one ink, with toothed clamp jaws), a cylinder flashlight, a folded blanket as three stacked rounded rects with a stripe, a water bottle, an ice scraper (trapezoid blade on a handle), a snow brush (handle with a bristle block), a small sand bag tied at the neck, a charging cable loop.

Generic unbranded car in side or three-quarter view: a rounded body shape in paper fill with an ink outline, two window shapes in pale glass tint, two tyres as graphite circles with paper hubs, a small door handle line. Variants: frost tint on windscreen and roof with snowflakes; raised on a two-post lift; towing a small box trailer; a wordless sign (rect with blank lines) in the rear side window; driver door open showing the door-jamb sticker.

Front view of a generic car: a wide rounded body, windscreen as a pale trapezoid, two round headlamps, a simple grille slot without any badge, a licence-plate rect under the grille, tyres as two dark blocks at the bottom corners. A taller boxy variant stands in for the van.

Two vertical posts in steel grey either side, each with a short arm reaching under the car's sills; the car raised above head height; the garage bay behind as a ribbed roller door (horizontal lines) and a darker floor band.

A small box trailer behind the car: rectangle body, single wheel, A-frame tongue to a ball hitch; light dust puffs (overlapping soft circles) behind the wheels and a flat sun disc with short rays in the sky.

A clipboard (rounded board with a metal clip at the top: rounded rect plus a small arc) holding a page with an eyebrow line, the title 'Service Boundary' in accent, two labelled field boxes side by side, a 'REQUESTED TODAY' label over two or three rows with hairline rules, a shaded box near the foot containing the not-authorized lines and a blank ceiling field, and two short initials lines at the very bottom.
A countertop edge as a long horizontal band with a darker front face; a service bell (dome with a small knob on a flat base) and a cup of pens as optional small props.
A round split ring with two simple keys (a round head with a hole and a notched blade) and one fob; optionally a manila repair-shop key tag on a short string loop.

Manila repair-shop key tag: a rectangle with the top corners cut off, a reinforced hole as a small ring at the top, a string loop; tag fill is the soft accent tone; words written on the tag in the monospace face, like a shop's tag.

Spiral-bound notebook page (a row of small loops along the top) or a loose ruled sheet, rotated about 3 degrees; column headers in small uppercase monospace with hairline column rules; filled rows in monospace, blank rows left as rules for a pen; year divider rows as an accent rule with the year beside it.

An A4 sheet with a small uppercase eyebrow 'VEHICLE MAINTENANCE COMPANION', the title 'Service record' in accent, a vehicle line, and a five-column table (DATE, MILES, WORK DONE, BY, COST) with hairline rules, oldest row first.

A small card with a dashed cut border and a scissors glyph at one corner (two loops with crossing blades); the title 'Glove box card'; label column in small uppercase muted text and a ruled value column, most lines left blank for a pen.
A manila folder with a tab, slightly open, with three receipts sticking out; each receipt a narrow white strip with a zig-zag torn bottom edge and a few short lines.

Rounded rectangle with a raised border (inner offset rect), two screw holes as small circles near the top, a thin top band left blank (no state or country name), large uppercase characters in a plate-like condensed face. Characters are only ever a vehicle label from the product's own demo data or the pin's own headline, never a real-looking registration number.
A small circle beside a plate chip in three states from the product: filled dot (something is due), ring (something is close), empty thin ring (clear).
Tear-off calendar page: a rectangle with an accent top band, two ring holes, and a grid of small squares; one square circled by hand. No specific date unless the pin's content gives one.
A dashboard rocker switch: a rounded rectangle housing with a tilted paddle, one end marked OFF in small uppercase; its on state shows the paddle flipped and a small accent glow.
The edge of an open driver door: a vertical strip of door frame with a small rectangular placard stuck to it, the placard showing a tiny tyre outline and blank lines.

A kitchen drawer pulled half open (front panel with a bar handle, sides in perspective) with a blue folder lying inside, its tab sticking up; the only blue in the vehicle set, taken from the guide's own 'kitchen drawer, blue folder'.
A simple ballpoint: a long rounded rect barrel, a clip line, a conical tip; laid diagonally across a page.

A plain phone frame (rounded rect with a thin bezel, no brand) holding one of the product's real captures from creative/public/screens/ (vehicle-maintenance-companion-vehicles.png, -history.png or -printables.png), cropped to the card the pin is about. Never a drawn or mocked screen.

visualWorld.palette: Built on the product's own accent so the pins and the app read as one thing: burnt amber #b45309 (dark-mode partner #f2a04a) as the single accent, the colour of an amber dash lamp and a manila shop tag; soft #fbe8d5 and wash #fdf3e8 for fills and tags; the printables' ink #211f1a, muted #6f6c62, hairline #e2e0d8 and paper #f4f3ee/#ffffff; graphite (ink at about 85 percent) for tyres, road, dashboard and counter. Winter pins add only a pale frost (white over the wash, stippled), never icy-blue backgrounds. One exception: the blue folder in home-drawer, because the guide names it. No alarm red anywhere.
visualWorld.mood: Calm workshop, in writing. Practical, tidy, daylight; the feeling of having the paper ready before you hand over the keys. Never panic, never 'your car is in danger', never a lit warning lamp. Headlines set in a sturdy heavy sans (not the serif of the current template), every number, date and field label in the monospace the product itself uses for mileage and dates, small uppercase letter-spaced labels like the printables' field labels.

archetypes.name: The page at the shop counter
archetypes.clicks: Printable mockups (a real page you can hold) are the dominant visual for car paperwork on Pinterest and Etsy, and 'car repair tips / mechanic tips / car tips for women' searches want something to bring to the counter. A clipboard on a counter with a car up on the lift behind it is the exact moment people dread, so it stops the scroll; the page itself is the save.
archetypes.layout: 1000x1500. Small tag line at y 70-110, left-aligned at x 64. Headline y 120-380, max three lines, heavy sans in ink. Visual y 400-1290: the counter edge as a band at y 1130-1290; the clipboard tilted -4 degrees, about 640x860, centred slightly left (x 120-760, y 420-1280) and overlapping the counter; in the top-right behind it, cropped and at reduced contrast, the garage bay with the car up on the lift (x 640-1000, y 400-760). Key ring with a manila key tag on the counter at x 60-260. On product pins, a phone with the real printables screenshot overlaps the clipboard's right edge (x 640-940, y 760-1240), ending above y 1260 so the lower-right corner stays clear of Pinterest's own icons. Product line bottom-left y 1360-1430: 'Vehicle Maintenance Companion' and 'Draftpace' in small type; the lower-right 240x200 is left empty.
archetypes.visual: Clipboard with the Service Boundary page, shop counter, key ring and manila tag, car on a two-post lift in the background, optional real printables screenshot.
archetypes.text: On the page only the real Service Boundary strings from printables/generateServiceBoundary.tsx: 'Service Boundary', 'Shop', 'Call me on', 'REQUESTED TODAY', 'Anything not listed above is not authorized.', 'please call me before any further work begins, and wait for my answer', 'Please do not go over, without a call', 'Owner initials', 'Shop initials'. Requested rows use job names from the printables screenshot (Oil and filter change, Tyre rotation). The ceiling field is left blank or carries the screenshot's own placeholder.
archetypes.bestFor: Mechanic and repair-shop pins, the Service Boundary, the 'while we had it up on the lift' Maple pin.

archetypes.name: The log page on the passenger seat
archetypes.clicks: 'Car maintenance log printable' is an established Pinterest and Etsy format: a ruled page with date, mileage, service and cost columns, often shown in a binder or on a desk. Infographic and printable pins earn saves because people want to keep the information (one agency A/B test reported 35 percent more saves for infographic pins). The ruled columns read as 'a log' even at thumbnail size.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 80-360 across the full width. The page (a spiral notebook page, an A4 service record, a glove box card or a 'From your manual' table) fills y 390-1300, about 820 wide, rotated -3 degrees, on a softly tinted surface (car seat fabric suggested by a few stitched seam lines at the edges). Column headers in small uppercase monospace; three to five filled rows in monospace; the rest left as blank rules for a pen. A pen lies diagonally across the lower-left of the page. On product pins, a phone with the real history or vehicles screenshot overlaps the left edge (x 40-340, y 820-1280). Product line bottom-left; lower-right corner clear.
archetypes.visual: A ruled log or printed record seen from slightly above, a pen, sometimes receipts or a manila folder peeking from under it.
archetypes.text: Column names and rows copied from the real printables (generateServiceRecord.tsx, generateGloveBoxCard.tsx), the product UI (VehicleForms.tsx, DueScreen.tsx), the demo data visible in the real screenshots, or the guides' own example tables, which the guides label as made-up examples; when a guide example is used, a small 'example' label sits above the table.
archetypes.bestFor: Car maintenance log, service record for a buyer, glove box card, manual intervals, paperwork tracker, winter log entry, first record.

archetypes.name: The odometer and the road ahead
archetypes.clicks: Mileage schedules (the '30-60-90' style chart) and step-by-step timelines are the niche's staple saveable infographic, and the odometer is the one number every driver recognises. A road with mile-marker posts turns any ordered list into a picture that reads top to bottom on a phone.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 80-300. The instrument cluster across the full width at y 320-660 with the odometer rollers as the focal point (or blank rollers when no real number belongs there). From under the cluster a road ribbon winds down to y 1320 in two soft S-curves; three to five mile-marker posts sit alternately left and right of the road, each with a label block beside it (monospace label in accent, one line of real text in ink). A small car shape travels on the road near the top. Product line bottom-left; the road ends before the lower-right corner.
archetypes.visual: Instrument cluster with odometer and fuel gauge, the windscreen-sticker in a corner where relevant, the mileage road with marker posts.
archetypes.text: Timeline steps copied from the guides' timeline and ordered-list blocks; typical mileage figures only from the mileage guide's own timeline and always captioned with its words 'Typical' and 'your manual wins'. Odometer digits are blank or come from the real screenshots' demo data.
archetypes.bestFor: Car maintenance by mileage, first week with a car, used car day one, history by year, usual jobs by fuel type, paperwork lead time.

archetypes.name: The glove box (or trunk), opened and labelled
archetypes.clicks: 'What to keep in your car', 'must haves in your car', 'car essentials for new drivers' and glove box organisation are evergreen list searches on Pinterest, often pinned by parents setting up a teen's car. A labelled flat-lay of real objects is the format those pins use; drawn flat, every item is legible at thumbnail size.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 80-340. A band of dashboard in graphite across y 400-540; the glove box hatch dropped open below it (x 140-860, y 540-1100) with contents fanned out over the hatch edge. Thin leader lines run from each item to a label in two columns (left x 40-300, right x 700-960). Optional 'keep at home' strip at y 1140-1300: a kitchen drawer with the title and spare keys. For the winter variant the same layout uses the open trunk instead of the glove box. Product line bottom-left; labels stop above y 1300 on the right.
archetypes.visual: Glove box with registration card, insurance card, owner's manual, roadside card, tyre pressure gauge, pen and notepad, glove box card; or the trunk with the winter kit.
archetypes.text: Item names copied from the glove box guide's tables ('What is worth having in the car', 'What is better kept at home'), RENEWAL_INFO in renewals.ts, or the pin's own description.
archetypes.bestFor: Glove box organisation, where the paper is, owner's manual first, handing the car over, 'everything in one place'.

archetypes.name: The car, with numbered callouts
archetypes.clicks: Car infographic boards on Pinterest are built around labelled diagrams: a car or an engine bay with numbered parts and short notes ('diagram of under the hood', car maintenance basics infographics). It is the niche's most recognisable infographic shape and it turns a checklist into something you can point at on your own car.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 80-330. The car drawn large (about 880 wide) in side or three-quarter view at y 400-1000, in the variant the topic needs: frosted with the boot open, on a two-post lift, towing a trailer in dust, a wordless sign in the window, the driver's door open. Numbered accent circles sit on the parts, each with a leader line to a label block; labels in two columns at y 1030-1310 (or around the car when there are three or fewer). Optional real screenshot as a small inset at upper right on product pins. Product line bottom-left; the right-hand label column ends above y 1300.
archetypes.visual: Generic unbranded car plus the parts the topic is about: battery-frost, tyre, wiper, washer-fluid, winter-kit, door-jamb-sticker, trailer, car-lift.
archetypes.text: Callout labels copied verbatim from the guides' tables and checklists (the winter table's 'Check' column, the first-car 'What to check on day one' list, the paperwork table) or the pin's own description; never more than eight callouts.
archetypes.bestFor: Winter prep, first car day one, used car first week, severe duty, selling the car, paperwork dates, what to say with the car on the lift.

archetypes.name: Side by side
archetypes.clicks: Two things next to each other read instantly at thumbnail size and answer 'which one?', the question behind two-car households, 'miles or months' and 'dealer or manual'. Comparison and 'say this, not that' layouts are a common infographic formula, and the two-panel split keeps the text short enough for a phone feed.
archetypes.layout: Headline y 80-330. Two panels (or three or four tags on one key ring) from y 380 to 1240 split by a thin vertical rule or a road centre-line; each panel has its prop at the top (a car from the front with its plate, an odometer dial or a calendar page, a manila key tag, a glove box or a kitchen drawer), a bold monospace label, and one to three short real lines. A shared line spanning both panels at y 1260-1320 states the rule they share. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Two cars from the front (sedan and van, or the demo 'Family car' and 'Commuter'), odometer versus calendar, two manila key tags, glove box versus home drawer, the dealer's clipboard versus the owner's manual, four key tags on one ring.
archetypes.text: Labels and lines from the guides' example tables, compare blocks and scripts, STARTER_LISTS names and blurbs, the vehicles screenshot, or the pin's description.
archetypes.bestFor: Two cars, miles or months, known versus unknown history, starter lists, in the car versus at home, reminders off versus on, dealer versus manual, request versus 'have a look at it'.

archetypes.name: Headline on a licence plate
archetypes.clicks: A licence plate is the fastest 'this is about my car' signal at thumbnail size, and Pinterest guidance favours a short, high-contrast overlay of a few words. Putting the headline on the plate makes the type itself the car-world object; a strip of smaller plates with lamps underneath shows the product's real plate strip.
archetypes.layout: Small tag line y 70-110. One large licence plate (about 860x420) at y 180-600 carrying the headline in uppercase plate type, up to three short lines (pins with long titles use a cut that keeps the title's words). Under it, y 680-1000, either a strip of two or three smaller plate chips each with a plate-lamp, or a single plate with a manila tag hanging from a screw hole. Supporting real line y 1060-1260 in sans, with any UI wording in monospace. Product line bottom-left.
archetypes.visual: Licence plates (characters are vehicle labels or the headline, never registration-like numbers), plate lamps in the three real states, manila tag.
archetypes.text: Headline on the plate; chip labels from the real screenshots ('ALL', 'Family car', 'Commuter'); lamp meanings and supporting lines copied from the two-cars guide, DueScreen.tsx or the pin's description.
archetypes.bestFor: The strip of plates, adding a vehicle, glove box details, 'nothing is due', 'nothing is assumed'.

pins.title: Car Maintenance by Mileage: Start With Your Owner's Manual

items: Every 5,000 to 6,000 miles: Oil and filter, tire rotation, a look at tread and pressure.
Every 12 months or so: Brake inspection, cabin and engine air filters, battery test.
Around 30,000 miles: Brake fluid and fuel filter, if your car has one to change.
Around 60,000 miles: Coolant, transmission fluid and spark plugs.
Around 90,000 miles: Timing belt, on engines that have a belt rather than a chain.
Typical. Where the two disagree, your manual wins.
content.source: src/content/guides.ts, guide car-maintenance-by-mileage-start-with-your-manual, timeline 'The same jobs, in the order they come round' and opening paragraph; same figures as MAINTENANCE_TEMPLATES in vehicleKnowledge.ts (always labelled typical)
